release_history_ahb.change: Update for AMBA 5 AHB Protocol Specification (Confidential)

New features and enhancements: Signal width properties, Write strobes, User signaling update, Signal validity rules, Interface protection using parity. Regularized terminology to Manager and Subordinate.

release_history_apb.change: First release for v2.0 (adds PPROT + PSTRB)

protocol_variants_described: AHB-Lite (single-Manager pipelined high-performance bus, Issue A)
AHB5 (extends AHB-Lite with optional secure / exclusive / user / parity features, Issue B onwards)
AHB (Issue C C terminology supersedes Master/Slave with Manager/Subordinate)
APB2 (AMBA 2 APB Specification, basic two-phase peripheral bus)
APB3 (AMBA 3 APB v1.0 — adds PREADY wait states and PSLVERR error response)
APB4 (AMBA APB v2.0 — adds PPROT protection and PSTRB write strobes)
fields.purpose: Defines the AMBA AHB and APB on-chip bus protocols. AHB is a high-performance, pipelined, synchronous bus suitable for memory-bandwidth-intensive Managers/Subordinates; APB is a low-cost, low-power, non-pipelined peripheral bus optimized for register-mapped peripheral access. APB is normally connected to AHB through an AHB-to-APB bridge. Both are members of the AMBA family (which also includes AXI/ACE).
key_features_ahb: Configurable data widths (HWDATA / HRDATA width: 8/16/32/64/128/256/512/1024 bits)
Pipelined address phase + data phase (overlapping addresses with previous data)
Single-Manager block + decoder + multiplexor (centralized for multi-Subordinate systems)
Subordinate-driven HREADYOUT (and chained HREADY) for wait-state insertion
Two-cycle ERROR response via HRESP (two cycles: HRESP=1+HREADY=0 then HRESP=1+HREADY=1)
AHB5 optional: Secure transfers (HNONSEC), Exclusive transfers (HEXCL/HMASTER/HEXOKAY), Extended memory types (HPROT[6:0]), User signaling, Interface protection using parity
key_features_apb: Not pipelined — every transfer takes at least two PCLK cycles
Two-phase transfer: SETUP (PSEL=1, PENABLE=0) → ACCESS (PSEL=1, PENABLE=1) → IDLE
Up to 32-bit PADDR and PWDATA / PRDATA
PREADY (APB3+) allows Subordinate to extend ACCESS phase with wait states
PPROT[2:0] (APB4) for normal/privileged + secure/nonsecure + data/instruction access
PSTRB[3:0] (APB4) write strobes for sparse-write byte-lane updates
Can interface with AHB, AHB-Lite, AXI, AXI4-Lite via an AHB-to-APB or AXI-to-APB bridge

ahb_htrans_types.name: IDLE
ahb_htrans_types.description: No data transfer; Subordinate must give zero-wait-state OKAY and ignore

ahb_htrans_types.name: BUSY
ahb_htrans_types.description: Manager continuing a burst but cannot complete next transfer immediately; Subordinate must give zero-wait-state OKAY and ignore

ahb_htrans_types.name: NONSEQ
ahb_htrans_types.description: Single transfer or first transfer of a burst; address unrelated to previous transfer

ahb_htrans_types.name: SEQ
ahb_htrans_types.description: Remaining transfers in a burst; address related to previous transfer

fields.ahb_4kb_burst_rule: An incrementing burst (INCR / INCRn) must not cross a 1KB address boundary (note: AHB uses 1KB not the AXI 4KB).
fields.endianness: Not endian-defined at the protocol level; byte-invariant when interfacing to byte-invariant systems (AHB Chapter 6).
fields.intended_audience: Hardware and software engineers who want to become familiar with the AMBA AHB and APB protocols and design systems and modules that are compatible with them.
fields.package_info_rationale: AHB + APB are bus protocol specifications, not packaged ICs. No package/pinout/electrical-DC data exists in these documents.
fields.electrical_specs_rationale: Both protocol specs define only logical signal semantics — synchronous, sampled on rising HCLK / PCLK; HRESETn / PRESETn active-LOW. No voltage / current / IO-standard information.

06 June 2006 / A / First release for v1.0; 25 June 2015 / B.a / Update for AMBA 5 AHB Protocol Specification; 30 October 2015 / B.b / Confidential to Non-Confidential Release; 15 September 2021 / C / New features and enhancements: Signal width properties, Write strobes, User signaling update, Signal validity rules, Interface protection using parity. Regularized terminology to be Manager and Subordinate.

AMBA AHB is a bus interface suitable for high-performance synthesizable designs. AMBA AHB implements the features required for high-performance, high clock frequency systems including: Burst transfers; Single clock-edge operation; Non-tristate implementation; Configurable data widths; Configurable address widths.
HSIZE[2:0]: 0b000=8 bits Byte, 0b001=16 Halfword, 0b010=32 Word, 0b011=64 Doubleword, 0b100=128 4-word line, 0b101=256 8-word line, 0b110=512, 0b111=1024.
HBURST[2:0]: 0b000 SINGLE, 0b001 INCR, 0b010 WRAP4, 0b011 INCR4, 0b100 WRAP8, 0b101 INCR8, 0b110 WRAP16, 0b111 INCR16.
Managers must not attempt to start an incrementing burst that crosses a 1KB address boundary.

The Advanced Peripheral Bus (APB) is part of the Advanced Microcontroller Bus Architecture (AMBA) protocol family. It defines a low-cost interface that is optimized for minimal power consumption and reduced interface complexity. The APB protocol is not pipelined ... Every transfer takes at least two cycles.
IDLE PSELx=0 PENABLE=0; SETUP PSELx=1 PENABLE=0; ACCESS PSELx=1 PENABLE=1 (waits while PREADY=0).
